predecessors.name: Han Song
predecessors.text: Jiangnan Province, whose head Han Lin'er made Zhu in May 1356

successors.name: Ming dynasty
successors.text: with Zhang Shicheng's Wu and Fang Guozhen's coast, all taken by December 1367

rulers.name: Zhu Yuanzhang
rulers.title: Duke of Wu (1361), King of Wu (4 February 1364)

ledger.x: April 1356: Zhu Yuanzhang takes Jiqing and renames it Yingtian.
1358-1359: Zhu holds four inland Zhejiang prefectures.
By the start of 1360 (bridging): southwestern Jiangsu and Anhui south of the Yangtze.
1361: Han Lin'er appoints Zhu Duke of Wu (Wu Guogong).
1361: Zhu takes Jiujiang from the Han, the Han retake it, and Zhu's fleet takes it again in September.
1361 (before August): Zhu captures Jiujiang from the Han.
August 1361: the Han counter-offensive retakes Jiujiang and Anqing.
September 1361: Zhu's fleet defeats the Han fleet and takes Jiujiang; it fails to take Hanyang.
Early 1362: Nanchang surrenders and Zhu holds Jiangxi.
March 1363 (bridging): Zhu's army relieves Anfeng.
June 1363 or later (bridging): Han Lin'er's court is housed at Chuzhou.
1364: the war with Zhang Shicheng's Wu begins.
4 February 1364: Zhu proclaims himself King of Wu (Wu wang).
March 1364: Chen Li surrenders Wuchang and Zhu begins to absorb the Han lands.
March 1364: the fighting with the Han ends at Wuchang.
April 1365: the Han lands of Hubei and Hunan are absorbed.
1366 (bridging): the rest of Wu's land north of the Yangtze and in Zhejiang.
24 April 1366: Zhu takes Gaoyou.
December 1366: Zhu captures Hangzhou.
January 1367: the Song court at Chuzhou ends.
1 October 1367: Suzhou falls after a ten-month siege and all of Wu was pacified.
1 October 1367: the war with Zhang's Wu ends.
October 1367: Zhu's armies attack Fang Guozhen's coast.
October to December 1367: Taizhou (October), Wenzhou (November) and Ningbo (Tang He's fleet) fall; Fang surrenders in December.
December 1367: Fang Guozhen surrenders; Zhu controls the entire coast (Hongwu Emperor page).
23 January 1368: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming at Yingtian.

wars.name: Chen Youliang's war with Zhu Yuanzhang (Battle of Lake Poyang)
wars.outcome: Zhu wins: Jiujiang 1361, Jiangxi 1362, Lake Poyang 30 August to 3 October 1363, Wuchang March 1364, the Han lands absorbed by April 1365.

wars.name: War of the two Kings of Wu
wars.outcome: Zhu wins: Gaoyou 24 April 1366, Hangzhou December 1366, Suzhou 1 October 1367.

wars.name: Zhu Yuanzhang's coastal campaign against Fang Guozhen
wars.outcome: Zhu wins: Taizhou (October), Wenzhou (November), Ningbo; Fang surrenders in December 1367.

wars.name: Red Turban Rebellions
wars.outcome: Umbrella conflict; Zhu absorbs Han, Wu and Fang and proclaims the Ming in January 1368.

certainty.note: City and prefecture holdings; the pages give the cities and circuits but no frontier line.
